newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian penis-shrinker death toll rises to three.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian penis-shrinker death toll rises to three.

text.p: Angry mobs have burned or beaten to death at least three alleged sorcerers in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan after a shrinking or disappearing penis scare spread from neighbouring Ghana.

Police said all the dead were African migrants, apparently Hausa, a major tribe in northern Nigeria with representatives in many West Africa countries. They were all lynched by mobs in Abidjan on Thursday.

Interior Minister Emile Constant Bombet, interviewed on state television's main evening news progranmme late on Friday, appealed for calm, telling Ivorians that the problem existed only in their minds.
"I appeal once again for understanding on all sides so that our brothers who have chosen to live in harmony with us in this country are at no time troubled (by such incidents)," he said.
"Openness has long been Ivory Coast's policy."
Bombet said such lynchings threatened to harm Ivory Coast's image in the world and compromise its reputation as a nation promoting peace and stability, needed for foreign investment.

Such reports are not uncommon in West or Central Africa. Purported victims often blame handshakes with sorcerers. At least 12 men were killed in Ghana in January by mobs accusing them of making penises shrink or vanish.

Police in Ghana and Ivory Coast dismiss the phenomenon as a ploy by thieves to cause a crowd to form and then rob people. Some victims say sorcerers touch them and make their penises to shrink or vanish to extort cash in return for a cure.
Ivorian police gave a death toll on Friday of two. They said on Saturday that a third victim had also been found. Crowds gathered in many parts of Abidjan on Friday to chase suspects.
